subject: maths
title: Functions & Transformations Adventure
welcome_lead: Final stretch: recognise standard graph shapes, shift and stretch them, and find the equation of any line.
meta_desc: GCSE Maths stretch — standard graphs, function transformations, and finding a line through two points.
final_note: You can spot common curves, apply transformations, and find the equation of a line through two points.

concepts.def: y = x², a U-shaped parabola through the origin
y = x³, an S-shaped curve through the origin
y = 1/x, two branches that avoid the axes
y = f(x) + a shifts the graph up by a
y = f(x − a) shifts the graph right by a
y = af(x) stretches the graph vertically by a

walkthroughs.body_html:
Learn these shapes by sight:

y = x² — U-shape through (0,0). y = x³ — S-shape through (0,0). y = 1/x — two curves in opposite quadrants.

y = √x — half-parabola starting at (0,0). y = 2ˣ — exponential, rising fast on the right.

y = f(x) + a: shift the whole graph up by a (down if a is negative).

y = f(x − a): shift the graph right by a (left if a is negative). Watch the minus sign!

y = af(x): stretch vertically by factor a. So y = 3x² is a steeper, thinner version of y = x².

Step 1: find the gradient m = (y₂−y₁)/(x₂−x₁). Step 2: substitute one point into y = mx + c to find c.

Points (1, 5) and (3, 11). Gradient = (11−5)/(3−1) = 6/2 = 3.

Use (1, 5): 5 = 3(1) + c → c = 2. Equation: y = 3x + 2.

mcqs.q: Which equation describes a U-shaped curve through the origin?
y = f(x) + 4 transforms the graph of y = f(x) how?

numericals.q: A line passes through (2, 7) and (5, 16). What is its gradient?

free_texts.q: Find the equation of the line through (0, 1) and (2, 7). Write as y=mx+c.
free_texts.hint: Gradient = (7−1)/(2−0) = 3. y-intercept is 1 (passes through (0,1)). So y = 3x + 1.
